ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: image1 is a sheet of paper composed of 3×3 small parallelogram cells, with 1 to 8 marked near the internal adjacent edges. image2 shows the same sheet of paper after being partially cut and folded: the middle region still forms a flat cross-shaped connected structure, and the four outer small cells are folded upward or downward along certain edges respectively; it can be seen that some adjacent edges are still connected as creases, and some adjacent edges have already separated into openings. Reasoning: Regard each numbered line as a possible connecting edge between two adjacent small cells. In image2, the four folded outer small cells are still connected to the flat cross-shaped part through creases, corresponding to numbered lines 1, 3, 5, 7 in image1, so these lines have not been cut. The edges adjacent to these folded small cells but shown as broken openings in image2 correspond to numbered lines 2, 4, 6, 8 in image1. The cuts must occur on these broken numbered lines.

raw_record.question_text: Lines are drawn on a piece of paper, and some of the lines are given numbers. The paper is cut along some of these lines and then folded as shown in the picture. Along which numbered lines were the cuts made?

method.method_draft: Describe the picture first: image1 is a 3-by-3 parallelogram grid with eight numbered internal seams around the noncentral adjacencies; image2 shows the same sheet after some seams have been cut and four outer panels folded upright/downward while the middle cross remains connected. Use an adjacency/hinge graph. Read from image2 which neighboring panels are still joined by fold hinges: the four upright panels are hinged to the flat cross along the seams corresponding to 1, 3, 5, and 7. The other adjacent seams around those same four panels are visibly open gaps, not hinges. Map those open adjacencies back to the numbered seams in image1; they are 2, 4, 6, and 8. Therefore the cuts were made along 2,4,6,8.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：image1 是一张由 3×3 个平行四边形小格组成的纸片，内部相邻边附近标有 1 到 8。image2 显示同一张纸被部分切开后折叠：中间区域仍形成一个平放的十字形连接结构，四个外侧小格分别沿某些边向上或向下折起；可见有些相邻边仍连着作为折痕，有些相邻边已经分开成开口。推理：把每条编号线看作两个相邻小格之间可能连接的边。image2 中，四个折起的外侧小格仍通过折痕连接到平放的十字形部分，对应 image1 中的编号线 1、3、5、7，因此这些线没有被切开。与这些折起小格相邻但在 image2 中表现为断开的开口的边，对应 image1 中编号线 2、4、6、8。切割必须发生在这些断开的编号线上。

method.method_draft: Describe the picture first: image1 has the numbered seams arranged cyclically around the outer band of the 3-by-3 grid, and image2 shows four raised or lowered flaps alternating around the central flat cross. Work around the numbered seams in cyclic order 1 through 8. In the folded figure, each outer flap must be attached to the rest of the sheet along exactly one seam and freed on the next seam so it can stand away from its neighboring panel. Thus, around the cycle, hinge seams and cut seams alternate. From the visible fold hinges in image2, the odd-numbered seams 1, 3, 5, and 7 are the retained fold lines; the alternating even-numbered seams are the free edges. Hence the cut seams are 2, 4, 6, and 8.
